**I have nothing on Toil & Trouble.** Neither the Joad client store nor the firm store mentions them, so I can't say what they want in case reports or how they sequence mediation and expert work. If they are another client, their preferences are probably confidential and shouldn't be used as a template for Joad without clearance. If you have their materials, send them and I'll compare.

Joad's own requirements are different and should drive the plan.

**Reporting (Joad)**
- A written report every six weeks, with a call after significant events.
- A first case assessment within 60 days, including an exposure range and a probability of an adverse result.
- A short note within five business days after every deposition.
- Ten days' notice of any proposed testing.
- All communications go to General Counsel Evander Thorsby.
- Perpetua Wallace (Cobaltridge) is copied on anything bearing on coverage and receives the monthly invoice summary.
- Joad wants same-day notice if the carrier reserves rights.
- Report any other JX-series spindle incidents immediately.

**Expert work (Joad)**
- Joad wants the names and credentials of all proposed testifying experts before engagement, so build clearance time into the retention timeline.
- Tell Joad whether anyone will speak to industry practice.
- Joad prefers design testimony to stay focused on the product at issue. It has offered to help identify candidates who have served on standards bodies.
- Get quotes and client approval before commissioning any testing, and clarify who pays for shared lab work.
- Provide a phase budget. Expert and testing costs usually drive most of the variance.

**Mediation and settlement (Joad)**
- The insurer pre-approved settlement up to $1,500,000, but that figure comes from an earlier matter, so confirm it for C-2.
- Anything above that needs written board sign-off, which takes about three weeks for the General Counsel to prepare. Flag this early.
- No offer above the insurer tier may be communicated, even as a signal, until the board's written sign-off is in hand.
- Even for an offer within the insurer's tier, consult Joad first, because the insurer will want to be involved.
- Do not rely on verbal indications from directors or officers.
- Do not stipulate to authenticity or business-record admissibility of Joad's test data until a protective order is in place.

**Suggested sequencing for Joad**
1. At intake, confirm settlement authority in writing, confirm the litigation hold, and calendar the reporting dates.
2. Interview key engineers early, but only after discussing with Joad. Go through Thorsby, and have no direct contact with employees.
3. Clear the expert candidates with Joad, then get testing quotes and 10 days' notice before any testing.
4. Deliver the 60-day assessment with the exposure range, then use it to decide whether and when to mediate, with board consent started in time if the range exceeds $1.5M.
